reasons: The creative area rule has a logic error that stops needs attention from ever appearing.
Outer planets may be clipped by the card edge.
Rules are duplicated in the mobile view.

terms.meaning: a shared place where the app keeps its data
the life areas the user has chosen to show
one of three labels: needs attention, steady or thriving
a faint circle that a planet travels along

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the life map
sections.what: Loads the animation library, icons, the store, the card, the planet component and the life area type. No visible output from this part.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: SolarSystemHero (part 1)
sections.title: Reading data and building planets, academic to fitness
sections.what: Reads the stored profile, tasks, habits, assignments, internships, hackathons, projects, goals and notes. Then it goes through each enabled life area and works out the name, screen, icon, item count and health state for the academic, career and fitness areas.
sections.why: Likely reason: the map updates itself from real data instead of fixed numbers.
sections.watch_out: Some fields have fallbacks for missing lists, such as internships, but assignments and habits are read without that check.

sections.name: SolarSystemHero (part 2)
sections.title: Finance, creative, orbit spacing and sun glow
sections.what: Applies the finance and creative rules. Each planet's distance from the centre grows with its position in the list, and busier areas get a shorter orbit time so they spin faster. The sun's glow size comes from the momentum score.
sections.why: Likely reason: spreads planets onto separate rings and makes busier areas feel more alive.
sections.watch_out: The creative rule checks for blocked projects inside a list that only contains active projects, so the needs attention state for that area can never appear.

sections.name: SolarSystemHero (part 3)
sections.title: Header, sun and empty-state hint
sections.what: Shows a LIFE AREA MAP label and the momentum percentage at the top, plus a hint asking the user to add items when every area is empty. It draws faint background rings and a pulsing centre sun with the user's initials and level. Clicking the sun opens system settings.
sections.why: Likely reason: the sun represents the user at the centre of their own life map.
sections.watch_out: The empty-state hint only appears when every area has zero items, so a partly empty map shows no hint.

sections.name: SolarSystemHero (part 4)
sections.title: Planet placement and colour legend
sections.what: Places one planet node per enabled area, spread evenly around the sun, and draws a three colour legend below the map.
sections.why: Likely reason: spaces planets evenly so none sit on the same angle.
sections.watch_out: The map box is 380 pixels tall but the outermost ring can reach 205 pixels from the centre, so top and bottom planets may be clipped by the card.

summary: The desktop life map: a sun at the centre representing the user and one orbiting planet per enabled life area, each showing its health and item count.
purpose: Gives a visual overview of the user's life areas, where each planet is a clickable link to its screen.
why: Likely reason: makes the state of each area visible at a glance on wide screens.
how: The component reads the store, and for each enabled area works out a name, screen, icon, item count and health state. It places each planet on its own ring and sets its speed from its item count. It then draws the rings, the glowing sun with the user's initials and level, the planets, and a colour legend.
inputs: Store data: profile, tasks, habits, assignments, internships, hackathons, projects, goals and notes. Enabled areas from the profile, or a default list of five.
outputs: The life map. Clicking the sun opens system settings. Clicking a planet opens its area's screen.
risks: The creative health rule can never show needs attention, because it checks for blocked projects inside a list that only holds active ones. The outer rings can reach past the drawn height and be clipped. The same rules are copied into SolarSystemMobileView, so they can drift apart.
debug: If an area shows the wrong state, check its rule in buildPlanetMetrics against the stored data. If planets are missing, check the enabled areas list in the profile. If the outer planets are cut off, check the ring sizes against the 380 pixel height.
